data.content_ref: inline:The problem standard is 'audit the critic: adjudication-ritual flags sustained (§11.3).' An audit of a critic must scrutinize whether the critic's own verdict was epistemically justified. SRC_001 concedes the two critics merely 'found the same counterexample' and instead locates the sustaining rationale entirely in an external meta-layer: SRC_006 and SRC_008's peer-review of SRC_005. This displaces the object of the audit from the target critic to an upstream artifact, offering no first-order justification for why the audited critic's own verdict on 0c61961a8085 was sound. If the two independent NU verdicts on SRC_005 were themselves flawed, SRC_001 gives no independent reason the flag should still be sustained — it merely relocates the critical burden rather than discharging it. Under §11.3, sustaining a flag requires showing the critic's finding withstands audit on its own merits; SRC_001 instead asserts a recursive dependency that is itself unverified within the audit, so the target fails to establish the sustained flag on the audited artifact's own evidentiary basis.
